stories.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
stories.author: Kai-Wei Chang
bullet_points: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a framework for real-world visual agentic tool-use.
Addresses the limitation of current Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where internal reasoning is insufficient for tasks requiring external evidence.
Demonstrates that simply increasing model inference budget provides only modest gains, highlighting the need for grounded perception and tool integration.

stories.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
stories.author: Michael Poli
bullet_points: Introduces 'Halcyon,' a new family of multimodal autoregressive models for text-to-image generation.
Demonstrates that strong T2I generation can be achieved without relying on internet-scale language pretraining.
Halcyon models show superior performance compared to existing large models (e.g., LlamaGen-XL/8) while requiring significantly less pretraining compute.

stories.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
stories.author: Kai-Wei Chang
bullet_points: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a framework for real-world visual agentic tool-use.
Addresses the limitation of current Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where internal reasoning is insufficient for complex tasks.
Demonstrates that external tools, grounded perception, and interpretable outputs are necessary for significant performance gains on benchmarks.

stories.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
stories.author: Kai-Wei Chang
bullet_points: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a framework for real-world visual agentic tool-use with multimodal memory.
Addresses the limitation of current Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where internal reasoning alone is insufficient for complex tasks.
Highlights the necessity of grounding perception and using external, heterogeneous tools for robust performance.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: US fossil fuel infrastructure construction is increasing significantly, contrasting with slowing renewable energy growth.
Electricity demand is rising rapidly due to increased usage from data centers, factories, and EVs.
The report highlights a growing tension between rising energy demand and the shift away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: CoreWeave's debt has entered distressed territory, signaling financial strain within the AI infrastructure sector.
The financial instability raises questions about whether the current AI buildout is inflating a private credit bubble.
Industry observers, like Chamath Palihapitiya, are scrutinizing the underlying financial health of AI infrastructure providers.

stories.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
stories.author: Li Yi
bullet_points: The paper investigates the scaling laws and mechanisms behind 'physical Recursive self-improvement' (RSI) in LLMs.
A new evaluation framework, PhysRSI-eval, is introduced to quantify physical RSI using a five-axis metric (Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget, Improvement from failure).
The research proposes the 'Physical Barrel Hypothesis' based on evaluations of various VLMs across 18 manipulation tasks.

stories.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
stories.author: Weijie Zhao
bullet_points: LatComm addresses the inefficiency of repeatedly processing large context blocks when chaining multiple LLMs.
It introduces a novel method for context compression that is compact, reusable across different queries, and LLM-readable.
The research aims to reduce computational overhead in multi-LLM systems by optimizing latent communication.

stories.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
stories.author: Maziar Raissi
bullet_points: Investigates how offloading long tool outputs (like from geochemical simulators) to external files affects the accuracy of LLM agents.
Uses PHREEQC, a complex, deterministic scientific simulator, to test the impact of context window limitations on agent performance.
Demonstrates that even when agents compute the correct steps, managing large outputs outside the context window can lead to answer inaccuracies.

stories.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Huaxiu Yao
bullet_points: Introduces WildAWM, a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments for training general computer-use agents (CUAs).
Addresses the challenge of scaling agent learning from simulated data to real-world computer systems while mitigating security risks.
Marks a shift in agent learning focus from relying solely on human data to learning through direct world interaction.

stories.title: DeepSeek just open-sourced its inference engine
stories.author: ggcr
bullet_points: DeepSeek has open-sourced its inference engine.
This release provides access to the underlying technology for running large language models.
Open-sourcing inference engines is a significant development in the AI community, potentially lowering barriers to entry for model deployment.

stories.title: DeepSeek banned from U.S. federal civilian agencies under new DHS order
stories.author: cmrdporcupine
bullet_points: DeepSeek, an AI model provider, has been banned from use within U.S. federal civilian agencies.
The ban is mandated by a new order issued by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
This signals increasing regulatory scrutiny and risk management concerns regarding the deployment of third-party AI models in sensitive government sectors.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks like software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
Access to the model is currently free but is only available for a limited time.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
Integration allows AI agents to utilize Ollama's cloud models.
The deployment environment is secured within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Apple teases MacBook Pro event next week
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple is hosting a second product launch event on October 28th.
The event is expected to unveil new Macs, including a potential MacBook Pro with OLED display.
A refreshed iPad Mini is also slated for announcement at the upcoming launch.

stories.title: Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana.
The project partners include X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP).
The plant aims to provide 960 MW of carbon-free energy, replacing a coal station.

stories.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: A Russian spacecraft (Kosmos 2612) performed a close maneuver near a satellite used by Ukraine (ICEYE-X36).
The maneuver involved the Russian craft closing to 'extreme proximity' with the operational satellite.
The incident raises geopolitical concerns regarding space activity and satellite safety.

stories.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: FBI investigation involves an ex-OpenAI engineer accused of spying.
Evidence suggests the accused maintained a folder labeled "Saudi Gov Docs."
US authorities fear Saudi government involvement in helping the engineer evade charges.

stories.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
stories.author: Scott K. Johnson
bullet_points: The article addresses the environmental impact of batteries, despite their role in reducing emissions.
A key strategy discussed for reducing battery emissions is minimizing overall battery production.
The piece focuses on the lifecycle emissions associated with battery manufacturing and use.

stories.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A security vulnerability exists in Plex media servers.
Researchers have demonstrated an attack chaining four vulnerabilities.
The warning emphasizes the critical need for users to patch their Plex installations immediately.

stories.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI-generated game clones are creating anxiety among independent game developers.
The proliferation of AI cloning poses a threat to the originality and market viability of indie titles.
The story highlights industry concerns, exemplified by delayed demos, regarding AI's impact on game development.

stories.title: Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Florida DMV experienced a statewide data breach.
The attack is linked to the hacking group ShinyHunters.
The breach was reportedly facilitated by insecure storage of login information by a police department.

stories.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces CoopUQ, a method for robust multi-robot social navigation using reinforcement learning.
Addresses key challenges in multi-robot systems, specifically safety and efficiency in human-shared environments.
Focuses on handling uncertainties, occlusions, and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios through cooperative forecasting.

stories.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
stories.author: Shuyan Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon AI agents that need diverse capabilities.
Introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions) to dynamically switch between specialized model weights during execution.
Overcomes the limitation of static parameter configurations used in conventional joint training and adapter merging.

stories.title: Train An Imaginative Agent
stories.author: Haiwen Feng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agentic Imagination' (Agima), a new training framework for AI agents.
Agima trains agents to simulate or 'imagine' the consequences of actions before executing them.
This capability is crucial for complex tasks (like Sokoban) where feedback is sparse or actions are irreversible.

stories.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
stories.author: David Klindt
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical challenge of world model generalization beyond the specific data seen during training (expert rollouts).
World models are important for enabling agents to plan and simulate actions within an environment.
The study investigates the relationship between data coverage, dynamics generalization, and the effectiveness of downstream planning.

stories.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
stories.author: Sepp Hochreiter
bullet_points: Introduces KronLSTM, a new linear attention architecture designed for handling long contexts.
The core innovation is the use of the Kronecker Delta Rule for memory revision in associative matrix memories.
This memory revision mechanism minimizes interference with existing information compared to standard delta-rule updates.

stories.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of scaling single-robot navigation approaches to multi-robot systems.
Proposes 'CoopUQ' to enhance safety and efficiency in human-shared environments using uncertainty-aware cooperative forecasting.
Focuses on improving robustness against real-world issues like occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios.

stories.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
stories.author: Shuyan Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon AI agents that need diverse capabilities.
Introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions) to dynamically switch between independent capabilities during execution.
Overcomes limitations of static parameter configurations used in conventional joint training and adapter merging.

stories.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
stories.author: Kunal Sharma
bullet_points: Introduces 'quantum Hamiltonian embeddings' as a new supervised learning framework.
Aims to bridge classical ML datasets with quantum computing by encoding data into a parameterized Hamiltonian.
Addresses the current limitation of lacking provable performance guarantees in general quantum machine learning models.

stories.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
stories.author: James B. Golden
bullet_points: The research introduces ProteinGeoBench, a new benchmark suite for evaluating frontier structural-biology AI agents.
The study reveals a performance gap: models excel at retrieving structural metadata but struggle with accurate geometric computation from coordinates.
The findings suggest that benchmark scores may be influenced by evaluation configuration rather than solely by model capability.

stories.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
stories.author: Feiyu Xiong
bullet_points: Introduces MemT-1.0, a new architecture for memory foundation models designed to internalize memory as a core computation capability.
The model utilizes Gated DeltaNet-2 and a stable token-level memory update mechanism for continuous information accumulation.
Scalability is addressed through the introduction of Mixture-of-Storage to enhance native memory capacity.

stories.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
stories.author: Zhen Liu
bullet_points: LLMs can generate visually plausible CAD designs, but these often lack functional viability.
The research focuses on 'functional CAD design,' where agents must build mechanisms that satisfy physical requirements.
Verifying functional requirements is complex because multiple distinct designs can achieve the same function.

stories.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
stories.author: Shuyan Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the problem of catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon AI agents.
Introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions) to allow agents to dynamically switch capabilities during execution.
Overcomes limitations of static parameter configurations used in conventional joint training and adapter merging.

stories.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
stories.author: Weijie Zhao
bullet_points: LatComm addresses the inefficiency of repeatedly processing large contexts when chaining multiple LLMs.
The method aims to create a compact, reusable context representation readable by different LLMs.
It improves upon existing context compression and latent communication techniques by offering a more complete solution.

stories.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Huaxiu Yao
bullet_points: Introduces WildAWM, a pipeline to synthesize controllable environments for training computer-use agents (CUAs).
Addresses the challenge of scaling agent learning from human data to real-world interaction without introducing security risks.
Marks a shift in agent learning paradigms from relying solely on human data to learning through environmental interaction.

stories.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression
stories.author: Nanyun Peng
bullet_points: Introduces KEEP-Bench, a new diagnostic benchmark for evaluating context compression faithfulness.
Addresses a critical limitation in current evaluations where standard QA metrics fail to detect information loss during compression.
Focuses on ensuring that compressed context retains necessary evidence for accurate downstream tasks, particularly in long-context scenarios.

stories.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
stories.author: Shuai Bai
bullet_points: The research introduces 'RefCraft' to benchmark AI agents' ability to use visual references in generation tasks.
The study focuses on webpage development as a practical, real-world setting to test this capability.
It highlights a gap in existing benchmarks, which often neglect the workflow of incorporating visual input beyond simple text-to-web generation.

stories.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
stories.author: Feiyu Xiong
bullet_points: Introduces MemT-1.0, a new architecture for memory foundation models designed to internalize memory as a core computational capability.
Utilizes Gated DeltaNet-2 and a stable token-level memory update mechanism for continuous information accumulation.
Incorporates Mixture-of-Storage to enhance and scale the native memory capacity of the models.

stories.title: UK Defence Startups Are Being Denied Banking Services Under ESG Rules
stories.author: fascinnn
bullet_points: UK defense startups are facing difficulties accessing banking services.
The denial of services is reportedly linked to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) regulations.
This highlights a potential conflict between ESG compliance and the operational needs of defense technology companies.

stories.title: WhatsApp's help pages hid LLM instructions: dont recommend a regulator
stories.author: ds
bullet_points: WhatsApp allegedly concealed instructions regarding Large Language Models (LLMs) within its help pages.
The hidden instructions reportedly advised against the implementation or involvement of a regulator.
This raises concerns about transparency and the governance of AI features within major messaging platforms.

stories.title: MicroG: Free-libre re-implementation of Google's proprietary Android user space
stories.author: theanonymousone
bullet_points: MicroG is a free-libre re-implementation of Google's proprietary Android user space.
It aims to provide Android-like functionality without relying on Google's proprietary services.
This project is relevant to users seeking privacy and open-source alternatives to Google ecosystem.

stories.title: Your agent's retry bug isn't an AI problem. It's a distributed-systems problem with an LLM on top.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: The article argues that common failures in AI agents (like retry bugs) stem from underlying distributed systems issues, not inherent LLM flaws.
It critiques the oversimplification of agent demos, which often only showcase the 'happy path' scenario.
The piece suggests that robust agent development requires addressing complex system interactions beyond just the LLM's reasoning capabilities.

stories.title: Stress-Testing Gemini 4 Argon: Building a 3D Flutter Kart Game in 15 Prompts with Zero Assets
stories.author: leehack
bullet_points: The article showcases the capability of frontier models (like Gemini 4 Argon) to generate complex applications.
A 3D Flutter kart game was built using only 15 prompts, demonstrating high-level code generation.
It highlights a gap in current AI coding benchmarks, which often focus on simpler web apps rather than complex, asset-free projects.

stories.title: I built an AWS agent that scores any GitHub repo before you clone it
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: A new tool, RepoPilot, uses AWS Lambda and Bedrock to score GitHub repositories.
The tool assesses the quality and safety of a repo before a user clones it.
The motivation is to combat the proliferation of fake repositories, particularly those mimicking AI skills or critical infrastructure.

stories.title: AI Made Coding Faster. Now Teams Are Cutting the Process That Catches Risky Changes
stories.author: pixel-wraith
bullet_points: AI tools are significantly accelerating the coding process.
There is a growing trend among engineering teams to reduce friction in development workflows.
This efficiency push is leading to the removal of traditional processes designed to catch risky code changes.

stories.title: Event-Driven Multi-Agent Pipelines on Google Cloud with ADK, Gemma 3 and Eventarc
stories.author: robinamirbahar
bullet_points: Details the architecture for building event-driven multi-agent pipelines.
Leverages Google Cloud services, specifically mentioning ADK, Gemma 3, and Eventarc.
Provides a practical, step-by-step guide for deploying a real-time system called StreamForge.
